text.p: Russian Olympian Vera Ilyina won the 1-meter springboard title at the 28th FINA/USA Diving Grand Prix Friday.
Ilyina, 23, won with a five-round total of 287.04 to top the six-diver field. She led every round.
Ilyina will also compete in the 3-meter on Sunday, the final day of the first major international meet since the Olympics where Ilyina finished seventh in the 3-meter.

"I was so disappointed after the Olympics," Ilyina said. "I knew I was a better diver. But that year our national team coach made us compete in 12 meets before the Olympics and I was very, very tired."

Ilyina is now coached by 1992 Olympian Matt Scoggin at University of Texas where she is majoring in international business. Six weeks ago she swept the 1-meter and 3-meter titles at the U.S. national collegiate championships in Indianapolis.

"I needed a change of scenery from Russia," Ilyina said. "It is not difficult to work with two coaches. It is the American food I don't like. There are no Russian restaurants in Austin, Texas. I have to drive to Houston on weekends for good Russian food."
China's Lei Cheng Wei and 1992 Olympic platform gold medallist Sun Shuwei were top qualifiers for Sunday's platform final. Olympic gold medallist Dmitry Sautin of Russia was third.
American Dean Panaro, a 1995 Pan American Games gold medallist on 1-meter in Mar del Plata, Argentina, withdrew from Saturday's 3-meter competition because of a career-threatening lower back injury.
"I had a really tough time diving in practice and I'm just not ready," the 25-year-old said. "This is as bad as it's ever been and I know there is someone else who can do a better job than me."
